title: Design a Top-K Trending / Real-Time Leaderboard System: given millions of engagement events per second, return the 100 most popular posts over a rolling 5-minute window, refreshed every few seconds, covering popularity definition, single-process baseline, Kafka ingestion partitioned by key, why local top-K then global merge is exact only with one owner per item, rolling windows, late events and event-time, duplicate handling, hot keys, approximate counting trade-offs, snapshot publication, serving layer, eligibility filtering, deterministic tie-breaking, and recovery.
shortTitle: Design a Top-K Trending / Real-Time Leaderboard System
keyPoints: Define popularity precisely (raw count, weighted score, velocity) because the whole system depends on it.
The single-process baseline is HashMap counts + size-K min-heap (O(N log K)); the distributed design scales this out.
Partition events by item key in Kafka so each item has exactly one authoritative counting owner.
Local top-K then global merge is exact only when each item has one owner; split counts miss globally popular items.
Rolling windows use event-time with watermarks and bounded lateness; deduplicate by stable event id.
Hot keys (viral posts) need partial pre-aggregation or key splitting to avoid overwhelming one partition.
Publish complete versioned snapshots atomically; the serving layer exposes freshness metadata.

s1_definition.oneliner: Partition by item so each has one owner, count in rolling event-time windows, dedupe and handle hot keys, then publish atomic versioned snapshots the serving layer reads with freshness info.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Top-K leaderboard** : ingests millions of engagement events and publishes the K highest-scoring items over a rolling time window.
- **Single-owner partitioning** : Kafka partitioning by item key so each item has exactly one counting authority.
- **Windowed aggregation** : hopping windows with event-time watermarks for correct time accounting.
- **Atomic snapshot publication** : writing a complete versioned result set and flipping a pointer, preventing stale overwrites.
- **Space-Saving / Count-Min Sketch** : approximate counting structures for memory-constrained environments.
s1_definition.analogy: National Bank of India runs a live dashboard of the 100 most-used features over the last five minutes, refreshed every few seconds. Millions of taps pour in. The system counts each feature's taps in a rolling window and publishes the top 100. The trick is making sure each feature is counted in exactly one place so totals are correct.

sections.s6_takeaway:
A real-time top-K leaderboard ingests millions of events per second and publishes the most popular items over a rolling window. I start by defining popularity precisely and build from the single-process baseline: HashMap counts plus a min-heap.

To scale, events flow through Kafka partitioned by item key so each item has exactly one counting owner. This single-owner property is the correctness crux: local top-K then global merge is exact only when counts are not split across workers. I use hopping windows with event-time watermarks, deduplicate by event id, and handle hot keys with partial pre-aggregation.

Publication writes a complete versioned snapshot atomically. The serving layer exposes it with freshness metadata so stale rankings are detectable. Filter ineligible items and break ties deterministically.

At National Bank of India, this powered a live dashboard of the most-used app features so product managers could see what customers were doing in real time.

Remember one sentence: partition by item key for single-owner correctness, count in event-time windows, deduplicate, handle hot keys, and publish atomic versioned snapshots to the serving layer.
